name: Polybox: both outputs wrong (F = 10, G = 10)
note: Same circuit and inputs, expected F = 12 and G = 12, but both outputs are observed as 10. The conflicts are {M1, M2, A1} and {M2, M3, A2}. M2 appears in both, so the single fault {M2} explains everything (it feeds both adders: Y = 4 instead of 6). The remaining minimal diagnoses need two broken components: {M1, M3}, {M1, A2}, {A1, M3}, {A1, A2}. Compare with the Polybox example, where F alone is wrong.
